newsitem.title: LATVIA: LAT DIPS, SEEN FIRMING ON GAZPROM DEMAND.
newsitem.headline: LAT DIPS, SEEN FIRMING ON GAZPROM DEMAND.

text.p: The lat lost a bit of ground to the dollar in early trade on Friday before firming and dealers said it was expected to climb next week if Russian energy giant Gazprom comes to town to buy part of its stake in Latvian Gas.
The lat opened at 0.5705/0.5710 to the dollar and eased to around 0.5720 before firming to 0.5713/0.5719, dealers said.
"Dollars were in demand earlier but it was speculative. There was big buying pressure in the morning but now the pressure has switched," said one dealer.
About $10 million had been traded on Latvia's currency market by midday, dealers said.
Dealers said they expected a surge in demand for lats next week ahead of Russian energy giant Gazprom's expected purchase of part or all of its 16.25 percent stake in Latvian Gas.
"They are only rumours at the moment, but it seems to be what the market is expecting," said one dealer.
German consortium Ruhgas and Preussen earlier this week bought 70 percent of its 16.25 percent stake in the Latvian gas distributor.
In the money market, overnight interbank activity was relatively slow and rates remained in the 1.5 percent to 2.5 percent range.
Dealers said this was a normal state of affairs at the end of the month when most banks have fulfilled their reserve requirements.
About 300,000 lats changed hands on the overnight market, dealers said.
